entries.definition: The report is the research prose written for a reader of the subject: one document from a lane's text to what the run assembles at its end, named by its stage only where the stage matters — your part of the report, the report as `show report` serves it, which is the only way a seat reads it, and the copy assembled for the human reader once the run is over.

allow.reason: ingest is the act that freezes the base, and its own help says what it builds
ingest's own refusals and result describe the base it builds

masks.reason: the synthesizer's own prompt: blue/report.md is that seat's file until ingest removes it
the synthesizer's own prompt, as above

masks.phrase: bash cp it to ${runDir}/blue/report.md, the one path ingest reads
masks.reason: the synthesizer's own prompt, at the write step: the path it copies its draft to before ingest

allow.reason: the synthesizer writes blue/report.md before ingest; it is that seat's file
the operator's run-directory map describes the synthesizer's file and its removal at ingest
ingest consumes blue/report.md and removes it; its refusal names the file it could not remove

collisions.resolution: a gap a lens is about to mint, screened by near-match, keeps the word; lane text is the report
blue/report.md is the synthesizer's file until ingest removes it; report.md at the run root is the assembled report

entries.definition: The run directory is the directory that holds one run: its record, its report and the documents assembled beside it.
The record is the run's account of every act, held as events in records/record.db, and every read a seat makes is a projection of it.

bans.variant: sitting, round, judicial, adversarial or process record

collisions.resolution: as a verb, say "put on the record" or name the verb that does it

entries.definition: A run is one research question taken from setup to its outcome.

collisions.resolution: debate.md, the Debate phase, `show debate` and the report's "The debate" section keep the word; the whole run is the run

entries.definition: An epoch runs from one chair sitting to the next: the chair relays who sits, the parties the record names sit, and the chair sits again.

masks.reason: a round-trip is a request and its answer, not a unit of the run

entries.definition: A sitting is one seat's dispatch, from the prompt the engine hands it to the envelope it returns.

bans.variant: your last turn, your next turn

collisions.resolution: a NULL TURN (a sitting that moved nothing on a gap) and an API turn (one model call inside a sitting) keep the word

entries.definition: An exchange is a red sitting followed by a blue sitting on one gap, and k-max counts them.
A seat is one agent's place in the run, registered under a seat id whose role decides the surface it is given.
A side is red or blue: red audits the report and passes or fails it, blue researches, writes and repairs it.

masks.reason: quotes a wrapper heading blue must not write; the prompt names the forbidden form, not a side

entries.definition: A lens is a red seat that audits the report for one class of defect, and the only seat that files findings and mints gaps.

collisions.resolution: a lane's source method is its method, never a lens

entries.definition: The chair is red's running seat: it relays who sits, rules blue's motions, spot-checks the stale areas before a PASS and records red's verdict.

collisions.resolution: blue's union of the lane drafts is a merge; the chair is the chair

entries.definition: The bench is the seat that adjudicates the contested docket, rules on motions and stamps how the run ended.

collisions.resolution: the seat ids judge, judge-terminal and judge-petition-* and the agent lead-judge keep the word; in prose it is the bench
the chair's is PASS when the board permits it; the bench's is whether remaining defect is worth remaining cost

entries.definition: A lane is one of blue's parallel first passes at the report, written by one researcher under one method.
The synthesizer is the blue seat that merges the lane drafts into the report by union and writes the report's authored surfaces.
The engine is the workflow script that dispatches the seats the record says are ready and reads the envelopes they return.

collisions.resolution: the Claude Code runtime a seat runs inside keeps the word

entries.definition: The operator is the person running the research, and the seat id their own commands run under.

The log is the entries a seat files for the operator with the `log` verb — a missing capability, a defect in the tooling, or friction, never a clean sitting, which is derived from having sat and filed no log entry — and none of it is debate material.

bans.pattern: \blog is (open — )?for friction\b|\bmet no friction\b|\bfriction (channel|log|footer)\b|\blog \([^)]*\) — friction\b|\b(collated|collected|aggregated|gathered) friction\b|\bfriction (so far|collected|collated|aggregated|gathered)\b|\bthe (run|sitting|seat|bench|chair)'s friction\b

collisions.resolution: `log` only ever writes; the operator reads the log with `ops log`

entries.definition: Friction is one type of log entry: something cost the seat a call, a guess or an act — a refusal, a guessed name, a misread shape, a workaround — and it notes what it expected and why, whether or not anything should change; an act no surface offers at all is a request, not friction.

bans.variant: impeded / impediment (the log read as blockage)

entries.definition: A missing capability is an act a seat needed that no surface offers, and it goes in the log, never on the board.
A citation is a source attached to a sentence of the report with the cite verb, hashed and dated so it can be checked again.

collisions.resolution: references/*.md and the proto's references option keep the word

entries.definition: A source span is the words a citation quotes from the source's own cached text, which the tool finds there once and keeps on the citation with the source's text around them; it is what the source says, and blue's reason for the citation is blue's account of it.

OCR-derived text is a machine's reading of a scanned document's page images: deterministic, and able to misread, so a citation quoting it records the PDF page its quote sits on and is checked against that page's image.
An anchor is the invisible token a citation, a proof, a finding or a gap leaves at its sentence in the report.
A proof is a recorded computation: a script that was run, with its hash and exit status.
A finding anchor is the anchor a lens's finding leaves at the sentence the finding is about.

collisions.resolution: the `.run-live` marker and the manual's `→ SHARED` marker keep the word

entries.definition: The verdict is the chair's PASS or FAIL on the board.
The outcome is how the run ended: VERIFIED, CEILING, HALTED or UNVERIFIED.
A finding is a lens's recorded observation of a defect in the report, or of a dispute with a gap already on the board, graded and not yet minted.
A gap is a defect in the report that changes a conclusion or a decision a reader makes, minted onto the board by a lens.

collisions.resolution: a parity gap between two numbers is ordinary English; a missing tool is a missing capability

entries.definition: A gap is material when its class is always material, or when its class goes by grade and its current severity is medium or above, and an open material gap holds the PASS gate.

collisions.resolution: material as content, or as bearing on the reader's question, is ordinary English; a gap is material only by its class and grade

entries.definition: A blocker is one entry on the list the verdict gate refuses a PASS on, with the seat whose act clears it.

collisions.resolution: `show work` marks an item blocking when the seat's sitting is not complete while it is open, and such an item is a blocker only when the verdict gate's list carries it

entries.definition: A contradiction is a source red read that refutes, or is silent on, a claim of the report, raised by the finding that names its id, and held open until a gap answers it — the gap minted from that finding, or an open gap that finding's lens credits with it — or until blue retires the citation it was read against, or that citation is checked against its sentence as it now stands and backed by every lens's latest check of it; the finding alone answers nothing, and a contradiction is not a report contradicting itself, which is the defect class `cross_section_contradiction`, anchored by quote.

collisions.resolution: a text at odds with itself, such as a report contradicting itself or a stamp that says the opposite of the board, keeps the ordinary word; the record's contradiction is the reading red recorded, whether its outcome is `refutes` or `absent`

entries.definition: To retire a claim is to take it out of the report with the retire verb, on the record.

collisions.resolution: a lens retires from dispatch, which is a state of the seat; a claim is retired from the report, on the record

entries.definition: Lens retirement is the record's state for a lens that has stopped finding material: three sittings in a row it sat through without a fresh material gap retire a lens that owes nothing on its work list — nothing new on a gap it minted since it last sat, no contradiction it read, no check it owns, no gap owed about a proof it judged unsound — and a head move does not ready a retired lens; a sitting stopped at the per-sitting call limit, or one that never closed, is not one it sat through and counts neither way.
A stale area is the area of a retired lens whose pin is behind the report head, which the chair reads and names in a spot-check before a PASS.

A report read is the record's evidence that the tool served a lens the whole report at a head, written by the report's whole read and by no read at an anchor or a selection; it says the text was served, not that it was read, and the head of a lens's latest one in a sitting it sat through is its pin, which the lens is readied past.

collisions.resolution: a dispatch's pin is the head the chair engages a party at; a lens's pin is the head of its latest report read in a sitting it sat through, and the lens is ready while the report head is past it

entries.definition: A disposition is the bench's ruling value on a docketed gap, and it decides whether the gap closes.

masks.reason: the carry verb's flag --carried-from, and its result as the archive view prints it: a closure carried from an earlier epoch

bans.pattern: \b(gaps?|dockets?) (that )?(you|the bench) (can )?carr(y|ies|ied|ying)\b|\bcarr(y|ies|ied|ying) (the gaps?|a gap|gaps|the dockets?)\b|\b(by|you|the bench|or|may|can|must) carr(y|ies|ied|ying) (it|them)\b|\bcarried (gaps?|dockets?)\b|\bcarr(y|ies|ied|ying)\b[^.]{0,60}\bdeadlock

collisions.resolution: an inquiry's state keeps the word
`carry` is the chair's verb that restates an archived closure, and the plain English sense keeps the word; the bench REMANDS a gap and never carries one

entries.definition: Grade movement is the change a regrade makes to a gap's severity, likelihood or impact, weighed as the difference in mass between the two grades in either direction, and once the open gaps' movement no docket ruling on its gap has followed totals more than 2.0 the dispatch dockets each such gap for the bench and a PASS waits for its ruling.

collisions.resolution: an exchange moves its gap when the gap's grade, its anchored text or its lineage changes or it closes, which is what impasse counts; grade movement is the regrade part of that alone, weighed in mass

entries.definition: A grade motion is a motion contesting a gap's grade, filed by any seat but the chair, which rules it.
A scorecard is the numbers a seat is measured on, computed from the record: red's for the lenses and the chair, blue's for blue's seats, the bench's for the bench.

collisions.resolution: a card is one of the three scorecards, red, blue or bench, and nothing else

entries.definition: A sitting's occasion is what it was convened to do — the question put to the seat, as against the seat id, which says who was asked — and only the bench carries one, because its four sittings share a single id.

collisions.resolution: "for want of occasion" in a log entry is the plain word and keeps it; the FIELD is the one a bench register carries

entries.definition: An inquiry is one question the research could take up — proposed by blue with the hypothesis that would be true if it paid off, recorded with what became of it, ruled on by the chair, and reviewed against the report once per epoch.

A citation or proof is reopened when an edit changes its sentence and no sitting opened since has checked it; its owning lens owes the check and is the seat readied for it — the evidence lens for a citation, the lens that owns proofs for a proof — a check by any lens from a sitting opened after the edit clears it, and a PASS waits until one does.

collisions.resolution: minting a successor over a closed gap reopens the gap, and a ruling's `reopens_on` says what would: neither is a reopened citation or proof
an edit's `reopened` lists every anchor its sentence change touched, of any kind, and `show work`'s `edited_since` reads it; only a citation or proof among them, checked before the edit, is reopened
